annotations.text:
EXPLAIN (TYPE DISTRIBUTED, FORMAT JSON) in Trinette.

All of it drawn on the query from the Trino docs — SELECT regionkey, count(*) FROM nation GROUP BY 1 — with the exact node ids, descriptors, details and estimates from that document. Nothing invented except where a caption says so.

Chrome is lifted from the real components: style.css tokens, the trino-dark monaco theme, the 18px toolbar band, DataViewer's field/value table.

The gap to know about before building any of this:

The JSON form gives you the per-fragment node trees and nothing else. The fragment header the text plan prints — Fragment 1 [HASH], the output partitioning, the output layout — is not in the document.

Everything shown with a dotted underline comes from there. Options: run the text EXPLAIN alongside, infer the partitioning from the $hashvalue projections, or drop the badges.

Three directions, same data, same size, each with its own case and its own cost.

A — fragments as boxes, dataflow left to right. The distribution is the picture.

B — one continuous tree, plan order, fragments spliced at the RemoteSource. Cheap, familiar, scrolls.

C — every node as a bar. Answers the real question, but the docs example has NaN for 8 of 9 nodes, which is shown rather than hidden.

If it were mine to build:

1. JSON tab. An afternoon, and it makes everything after it a rendering choice over data already on the client.

2. Option B. A TreeView and rows, no layout engine, and it is the view that survives a wide plan.

3. Option A as a second tab once B proves the parsing.

4. C as a column in B, not a view of its own.

The inspector is free either way — the pane already renders field/value pairs.
